title: Tax Owed Across Rate Bands
statement:
A tax table is given as bands, where bands[i] = [upper, percent]. The upper limits are strictly increasing. Band 0 covers income from 0 up to its upper; each later band covers income from the previous band's upper up to its own.

Each band taxes only the part of the income that falls inside it, at its own percent. Given income, which never exceeds the last band's upper limit, return the total tax owed. Answers within 10⁻⁵ of the exact value are accepted.

examples.why: The first 10 at 10% is 1, the next 20 at 20% is 4, the last 15 at 50% is 7.5. Charging 50% on all 45 would give 22.5.
The whole income sits in the first band, which is tax-free. The 15% band is never reached.

hints: Each band only sees a slice of the income. How big is the slice for band i?
The slice runs from the previous upper limit to min(upper, income). If the income is below the previous upper, the slice is empty.
Walk the bands in order, add slice × percent / 100, and stop once the previous upper limit reaches the income.

explain.intuition:
This is how progressive tax actually works, and the common mistake is the same one people make in real life: thinking that moving into a higher band raises the rate on everything. It does not. The 50% band only touches the money above 30 in the first example.

So treat the income as a bar cut into slices at the band limits. Band i owns the slice from prev (the previous upper limit, 0 for the first band) to min(upper, income). Tax that slice, move prev up, and stop as soon as prev reaches the income.
steps: For each band [upper, percent]: if income ≤ prev, stop.
pitfalls: Applying the rate of the highest band reached to the whole income.
Taxing a full band even when the income stops inside it. Use min(upper, income).
Using the band's own upper limit as its width. The width is upper − prev, not upper.

solutions.title: Unit by unit
solutions.idea: For each unit of income, find the band it falls in and add that band's percent. Simple, but proportional to the income.

solutions.title: Slice per band
solutions.idea: Each band taxes the slice of income between the previous limit and min(its limit, income).

followups: Many people query the same table with different incomes. Precompute something so each query is O(log n).
Given a target tax, find the smallest income that owes at least that much.
